# Predicting the probability of depression

Logistic regression on survey data from rural parts of an unnamed country
(n = 1,401 after cleaning). Three sequential models predict the probability
of depression from sex, age, marital status, education level and living
expenses. R 4.0.2. Packages used: tidyverse, ggalt, gridExtra, broom,
ggpubr, dplyr, car, psych, Hmisc, ggplot2, gmodels, DescTools, stargazer,
semTools, corrplot, Epi, lmtest, rcompanion.

---

```{r}
library(tidyverse) # general
library(ggalt) # dumbbell plots
library(gridExtra) # plots
library(broom) # significant trends within countries
library(ggpubr)
library(dplyr)
library(car)
library(psych)
library(Hmisc)
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(gmodels)
```

```{r}
## Loading dataset
depresseddata <- read.csv("../data/b_depressed.csv")

## Summary statistics
Hmisc::describe(depresseddata)

### Removing NAs
sum(is.na(depresseddata))
na.omit(depresseddata$Age)
depresseddata <- na.omit(depresseddata)

```

depresseddata$Age

### Descriptive stats for normality for each numerical variables

Education Level is normally distributed when we remove outliers.

https://www.introspective-mode.org/getting-the-hang-of-z-scores/

```{r}

x <- depresseddata$education_level
h<-hist(x,
 breaks=12,
 col="blue",
 xlab="Education Level",
 main="Distribution of Education Level")

xfit<-seq(min(x), max(x), length=40)
yfit<-dnorm(xfit, mean=mean(x), sd=sd(x))
yfit <- yfit*diff(h$mids[1:2])*length(x)
lines(xfit, yfit, col="red", lwd=2)
box()

## Removing outliers and re-plotting
Q <- quantile(depresseddata$education_level, probs=c(.25, .75), na.rm = FALSE)
iqr <- IQR(depresseddata$education_level)
up <-  Q[2]+2.5*iqr # Upper Range @ +/- 1.96 cut off
low<- Q[1]-1.5*iqr # Lower Range

educationountoutliers <- subset(depresseddata, depresseddata$education_level > (Q[1] - 1.5*iqr) & depresseddata$education_level  < (Q[2]+2.5*iqr))

x <- educationountoutliers$education_level
h<-hist(x,
 breaks=12,
 col="blue",
 xlab="Education Level",
 main="Education Level Distribution")

xfit<-seq(min(x), max(x), length=40)
yfit<-dnorm(xfit, mean=mean(x), sd=sd(x))
yfit <- yfit*diff(h$mids[1:2])*length(x)
lines(xfit, yfit, col="red", lwd=2)
box()

#skewness and kurtosis from semTools with standard error
tpskew<-semTools::skew(depresseddata$education_level)
tpkurt<-semTools::kurtosis(depresseddata$education_level)
#We divide the skew statistic by the standard error to get the standardised score
tpskew[1]/tpskew[2]
tpkurt[1]/tpkurt[2]

library(ggpubr)
ggqqplot(depresseddata$education_level)

shapiro.test(depresseddata$education_level)


```

### Differences and Correlations

```{r, eval= FALSE}
raqMatrix<-cor(depresseddata)
corrplot::corrplot(raqMatrix, method="circle", type="upper")
```

Depression is 0 = Depressed, 1 = Not Depressed

1. Sex is 0 = Male, 1 = Female

Chi Square tests for sex and depression
Chi^2 =  0.010     d.f. =  1     p =  0.922
phi = 0.003

```{r}
library (gmodels)
CrossTable(depresseddata$depressed, depresseddata$sex, fisher = TRUE, chisq = TRUE, expected = TRUE,sresid = TRUE, format = 'SPSS')

mytableSex<-xtabs(~depressed+sex, data=depresseddata)
ctest<-chisq.test(mytableSex, correct=TRUE)

ctest#will give you the details of the test statistic and p-value
ctest$expected#expected frequencies
ctest$observed#observed frequencies
ctest$p.value

library(DescTools)
phi.test <- Phi(mytableSex)  # the Phi function uses DescTools package
phi.test

```

Chi Square tests for marriage and depression

2. Married is 0 = Not Married, 1 = Married

The null hypothesis (H0) states: Depression is not associated of Marriage.

Chi^2 =  5.437     d.f. =  1     p =  0.0197

phi = 0.062

Since the p-value is less than our chosen significance level α = 0.05, we can reject the null hypothesis, and conclude that there is an association.
```{r}
library (gmodels)
CrossTable(depresseddata$depressed, depresseddata$Married, fisher = TRUE, chisq = TRUE, expected = TRUE,sresid = TRUE, format = 'SPSS')

mytableMarried<-xtabs(~depressed+Married, data=depresseddata)
ctest<-chisq.test(mytableMarried, correct=TRUE)

ctest#will give you the details of the test statistic and p-value
ctest$expected#expected frequencies
ctest$observed#observed frequencies
ctest$p.value

library(DescTools)
phi.test <- Phi(mytableMarried)  # the Phi function uses DescTools package
phi.test

```

#### Building our Logistic Regression Model - Baseline

Building the model itself

Likelihood ratio test: Chi^2 = 0.05 on 1 DF, p-value: 0.831

```{r}
library("car")
library("stargazer")

logmodel1 <- glm(depressed ~ sex, data=depresseddata, na.action=na.exclude, family=binomial())
logmodel1

summary(logmodel1)
stargazer(logmodel1, type="text")
```

Digging into the model a bit further
```{r}
## Looking at Pr(>Chisq)
## 0.8314
lmtest::lrtest(logmodel1)

## Test for pseudo R2 and chi square.
## R Squared is tiny
rcompanion::nagelkerke(logmodel1, restrictNobs = T)

## Exponential coefficients.
exp(coefficients(logmodel1))

## Plot a ROC curve and look for specificity and sensitivity.
## We want to look at the Area under the curve
## .5 is weak, .8 is strong
## AUC = 0.502

Epi::ROC(form=depresseddata$depressed ~ depresseddata$sex, plot="ROC")

## the table of deviance
anova(logmodel1, test="Chisq")

## Odds Ratios
library(dplyr)
odds<-depresseddata %>%
        group_by(depressed,sex) %>%
        summarise(freq=n()) %>%
        mutate(all=sum(freq),prob=freq/all,odds=prob/(1-prob),logodds=log(odds)) %>%
        round(.,5)
odds

## Zone in on Chi for the model to check for improvement
modelChi <- logmodel1$null.deviance - logmodel1$deviance
modelChi

## Zone in on Degrees of freedom for our model (will usually be 1)
## 5
chidf <- logmodel1$df.null - logmodel1$df.residual
chidf

## Zone in on Chi for getting the probability or no model pr baseline
chisq.prob <- 1 - pchisq(modelChi, chidf)
chisq.prob
```

#### Building our Logistic Regression Model - Model 2

Including Age and Marriage into the model

             Estimate  Std. Error  z value  Pr(>|z|)
Age65-91     0.8509     0.3186     2.671     0.0076 **

AIC: 1259.4

```{r}
library("car")
library("stargazer")

logmodel2 <- glm(depressed ~ sex + Age + Married, data=depresseddata, na.action=na.exclude, family=binomial())
logmodel2

summary(logmodel2)
stargazer(logmodel2, type="text")
```

Digging into the model a bit further

Fit for model

[1] 13.45
[1] 5
[1] 0.0195

```{r, eval = FALSE}
## Looking at Pr(>Chisq)
lmtest::lrtest(logmodel2)

## Test for pseudo R2 and chi square.
## R Squared is tiny at  0.0096 to  0.0161
rcompanion::nagelkerke(logmodel2, restrictNobs = T)

## Exponential coefficients.
exp(coefficients(logmodel2))

## Plot a ROC curve and look for specificity and sensitivity.
## We want to look at the Area under the curve
## .5 is weak, .8 is strong
## AUC = 0.550
Epi::ROC(form=depresseddata$depressed ~ depresseddata$Age, plot="ROC")

## Zone in on Chi for the model to check for improvement
modelChi <- logmodel2$null.deviance - logmodel2$deviance
modelChi

## Zone in on Degrees of freedom for our model (will usually be 1)
## 5
chidf <- logmodel2$df.null - logmodel2$df.residual
chidf

## Zone in on Chi for getting the probability or no model pr baseline
chisq.prob <- 1 - pchisq(modelChi, chidf)
chisq.prob

## Odds Ratios
library(dplyr)
odds<-depresseddata %>%
        group_by(depressed, Married) %>%
        summarise(freq=n()) %>%
        mutate(all=sum(freq),prob=freq/all,odds=prob/(1-prob),logodds=log(odds)) %>%
        round(.,5)
odds

#Collinearity
library(car)
vifmodel<-vif(logmodel2)
1/vifmodel
```

#### Building our Logistic Regression Model - Model 3

Including Education Level and Living Expenses into the model 3

education_level -6.07e-02  2.67e-02  -2.278   0.0227 *

AIC: 1257.7

```{r}
library("car")
library("stargazer")

logmodel3 <- glm(depressed ~ sex + Age + Married + education_level + living_expenses, data=depresseddata, na.action=na.exclude, family=binomial())
logmodel3

summary(logmodel3)
stargazer(logmodel3, type="text")
```

Collinearity: Values of VIF do not exceed 2.5 or are lower than 0.4

                     GVIF        Df GVIF^(1/(2*Df))
sex             0.8865069 1.0000000       0.9415450
Age             0.6897035 0.3333333       0.9399622
Married         0.7742340 1.0000000       0.8799057
education_level 0.7439319 1.0000000       0.8625149
living_expenses 0.9963813 1.0000000       0.9981890

Model of fit Chi Square

[1] 19.18 --
[1] 7 -- DF, how many variables + 1
[1] 0.0077 -- new model is significant ss it's closer to 0

```{r, eval = FALSE}
## Looking at Pr(>Chisq)
## 0.0077
lmtest::lrtest(logmodel3)

## Test for pseudo R2 and chi square.
## R Squared is tiny at 0.0136 to 0.0229
rcompanion::nagelkerke(logmodel3, restrictNobs = T)

## Exponential coefficients.
exp(coefficients(logmodel3))

## Zone in on Chi for the model to check for improvement
modelChi <- logmodel3$null.deviance - logmodel3$deviance
modelChi

## Zone in on Degrees of freedom for our model (will usually be 1)
## 5
chidf <- logmodel3$df.null - logmodel3$df.residual
chidf

## Zone in on Chi for getting the probability or no model pr baseline
chisq.prob <- 1 - pchisq(modelChi, chidf)
chisq.prob

## Plot a ROC curve and look for specificity and sensitivity.
## We want to look at the Area under the curve
## .5 is weak, .8 is strong
## AUC = 0.574
Epi::ROC(form=depresseddata$depressed ~ depresseddata$sex + depresseddata$Age + depresseddata$Married + depresseddata$living_expenses + depresseddata$education_level, plot="ROC")

#Check assumptions
#Cooks distance
cooks.distance(logmodel3)
#Plot Cooks distance
plot(cooks.distance(logmodel3), ylab='Cooks statistic')

#Create histogram
#A density plot of the residuals
resid(logmodel3)
plot(density(resid(logmodel3)))

#Create a QQ plotqqPlot(model, main="QQ Plot") #qq plot for studentized resid
leveragePlots(logmodel3) # leverage plots

#Collinearity
library(car)
vifmodel<-vif(logmodel3)
1/vifmodel

## the table of deviance
## Analyzing the table we can see the drop in deviance when adding each variable one at a time.
anova(logmodel3, test="Chisq")

## Odds Ratios
library(dplyr)
odds<-depresseddata %>%
        group_by(depressed, education_level) %>%
        summarise(freq=n()) %>%
        mutate(all=sum(freq),prob=freq/all,odds=prob/(1-prob),logodds=log(odds)) %>%
        round(.,5)
odds

library(dplyr)
odds<-depresseddata %>%
        group_by(depressed, living_expenses) %>%
        summarise(freq=n()) %>%
        mutate(all=sum(freq),prob=freq/all,odds=prob/(1-prob),logodds=log(odds)) %>%
        round(.,5)
odds

```
